title: GSB literal: rule faults found by the first skill run (Gen 5-6)
description: From the gsb-translate trial on Genesis 5-6 (overrides/01-gen.scm ;; Genesis 6). Fix in scripts/lib/gsb-literal.scm with tests: (1) accusative articular infinitive with its own subject, μετὰ τὸ γεννῆσαι αὐτὸν τὸν Σήθ 'after to beget him Seth' (Gen 5:4-30, 9 verses; also 6:3 διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτούς; Gen 3:19 pinned the same construction) -> 'after he begot Seth'; (2) subject after a participle not moved (6:2 ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ υἱοί, 6:5); (3) a genitive object moved with the subject: ἐπλήσθη ἡ γῆ ἀδικίας (6:11, 13); (4) articular subject after εἰμί not moved: ἔσονται δὲ αἱ ἡμέραι αὐτῶν (6:3); (5) attracted relative after an adjective (ἀπὸ πασῶν ὧν, 6:2) still 'of which'. Fixed already: relative matched to an indeclinable name (5:2, 5, 27), consonant doubling for beget/transfer (the 6:4#28 english override can now go).
close_reason: Fixed with tests: possessive gerund for preposition+τό+infinitive+accusative pronoun subject; participle subjects moved; εἰμί moves articular/name subjects; genitive object of (genitive ...) verbs stays; attracted relative after adjective; pronoun antecedent rule (thing → it); kai-joined warning. Left (ponytail, README): noun subject of an articular infinitive.

title: GSB literal: form analyses and glosses for the rest of Genesis and Exodus (batches of ~100 forms)
description: After the pilot (ursinia-vff.22): Genesis has 2156 distinct unanalyzed forms (3715 tokens) and 694 table lemmas not in glosses; Exodus 2010 forms (3634 tokens), 633 lemmas (./scripts/gsb-literal.sh stats gen exod). Workflow per batch: ./scripts/gsb-literal.sh todo <book> <chapters> gives form, count, table lemma, first ref, verse context; add rows to gsb/literal/forms/NN-<id>.tsv and lemma entries to gsb/lexicon/glosses.scm; generate; make gsb/literal/check; read the output and add overrides (gsb/literal/overrides/NN-<id>.scm) or generic rule fixes. Make this a skill (.claude/skills/gsb-literal) once the owner accepts the approach. Split by chapter ranges so agents touch different forms; glosses.scm is shared (appended block at the end, see next item).
notes: Skill .claude/skills/gsb-translate written and trialed by a fresh agent on Genesis 5-6 (65 form rows, 86 lemmas, 11 overrides, 0 pins; 135 tool calls, ~15 min, ~230k tokens). Recommended batch: 2 chapters per agent context.

title: GSB literal: owner rulings for the scripted layer (supplied articles/copulas, he/it heuristic, ὅς = which, shared glosses)
description: Pilot ursinia-vff.22 (gsb/literal/README.md). Decisions the generator makes that need the owner: (1) it supplies no English articles or copulas by itself ("In beginning", "darkness over the abyss"); hand drafts supply [the]/[a]/[was]; overrides add them one by one (31 of 66 Gen 1-3 overrides). Rule? (2) third-singular pronouns he/she/it are chosen by nearest earlier agreeing noun (person nouns flagged (person) in glosses); verb-ending pronouns unbracketed as in the hand drafts; repeated after every καί ("and he sanctified it"). (3) ὅς always "which", also for persons (hand drafts: "whom"). (4) present indicative simple present ("goes out"), hand draft progressive. (5) glosses that now share an English word: ἀγαθός/καλός good, οἶκος/οἰκία house, οὔτε/οὐδέ nor, ἥκω come; φέρω carry (ἄγω has bring). (6) ἡμέρα μία "one day" (generator moves adjectives) vs hand "day one".
close_reason: Owner ruled (rule 16a); implemented: no default supplied articles/copulas, he/she/it for unstated subjects (none after καί, gender only from the clause, impersonal list in data), his/its for masc/neut-ambiguous forms, who/whom via (person) antecedent. Overrides pruned.

title: GSB: our own CC0 transcription of Swete's Septuagint from public-domain scans
description: Owner decision 2026-11-25: no existing digital LXX is acceptably public domain (eliranwong Swete has a GPL claim; First1KGreek is CC BY-SA; Rahlfs/CCAT restricted; Brenton lacks Old Greek Daniel). We transcribe Swete ourselves from archive.org scans (vol I theoldtestamenti00unknuoft 1909/1925 Gen-4 Kgdms; vol II oldtestamenting02swet 1907 1 Chr-Tobit; vol III oldtestgreek00unknuoft 1912/1930 Hosea-4 Macc incl. Daniel), book by book ahead of translation, Genesis and Old Greek Daniel/Susanna/Bel first. Nothing is rendered for an LXX book until our transcription exists (owner chose no Brenton placeholder). Output: gsb/sources/swete/NN-<book-id>.tsv (chapter, verse, text as printed). Method to be settled by a pilot on Genesis 1-3 and OG Daniel 1: independent readings from the page images (archive.org OCR layer, fresh OCR, model reading of the image), collated, disagreements settled against the image and logged. Third-party transcriptions never enter the repo.
notes:
Pilot 2026-11-25 (method swete-pilot-1): Gen 1-3 + Dan 1 OG/Th transcribed into gsb/sources/swete/ (pages/, 01-genesis.tsv, daniel-og.tsv, daniel-th.tsv, provenance.tsv, decisions.tsv, README.md). Scripts: scripts/gsb-swete-fetch.sh (images+OCR to ~/.cache/gsb-swete, doctor), scripts/gsb-swete-verses.sh (pages -> verse TSV). Accuracy over 2,925 page tokens: archive OCR 86.2% words / 92.9% chars; fresh Tesseract grc 90.6% / 93.2%; direct image reading (first pass) 99.83% / 99.97% (5 errors, 4 caught by collation, 1 ambiguous). Yardstick (eliranwong, measurement only) on 2,885 verse tokens: 0 our errors caught only by yardstick, 2 yardstick errors, 1 genuine ambiguity (Gen 2:14 Ἀσσυρίων ,/.), 7 sigla-convention diffs. Hazards: rough vs smooth breathing on capitals (Tesseract reads smooth; Ἁνανίας, Ἁμελσάδ, Εὑειλάτ), hOCR merging first text line into running head, specks read as periods in vol III, Swete versification (his 3:1 = 2:25+3:1). Prototype extraction/collation code is Python in the session scratchpad only; port to Guile is a follow-up.

title: Greek Source Bible: own translation from LXX + Greek NT
description: Build our own English Bible translated only from Greek (Septuagint OT, Greek NT) and publish it under /bible. Decisions so far (2026-11-25): NT = critical base with TR longer readings restored and marked (Comma Johanneum etc.); LXX = all books stored/rendered in LXX order, deuterocanon flagged and translated last; both Daniel texts shown, Old Greek authoritative, Theodotion for comparison; traditional English proper names; two English layers per verse: hyper-literal first (YLT-level word order, one gloss per lemma per sense script-enforced, aspect rendered consistently, particles always rendered, supplied words bracketed incl. articles e.g. 'In [the] beginning'), essentially-literal readable layer second, pilot both on Genesis 1-3. Workflow: agent drafts chapter + decision notes, user reviews. Tooling in Scheme under scripts/, own Make target that site build depends on, project AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md (@AGENTS.md), skills for repeatable tasks, code-enforced conformance checks.

title: GSB Swete: make transcription audits provably blind and measure their sensitivity
description: Genesis audit 2026-11-26: 12 leaves (44,49,53,60,73,84,98,106,109,114,126,131), 3,655 words, 0 confirmed transcription errors; 7 reader errors where the file was right. But independence is unproven: the audit subagents' blind readings were byte-identical to the page file on 7 of 12 leaves with identical timestamps; only the lead auditor's own blind check (645 words, 0 file errors) can be vouched for (upper bound ~0.5%/word). All readers are the same model family, so shared blind spots are unmeasured. To do: (1) blind reader gets only the image and format rules, no repo path or decisions log, and its reading is saved where the comparer cannot change it; (2) seed 10-20 known errors into a copy of a page to measure detection rate; (3) mandatory crop for an oxytone at line end before a capitalized quotation on the next line; (4) require an 'ambiguous: broken type' row for any malformed glyph even when readings agree (leaf 126 line 6 apeggeilen has none); (5) lint decision basis text against the change recorded (leaf 126 Arabia row); (6) consider a human or different-model pass on a random 10% of lines for the diacritic layer. Build this into the gsb-transcribe skill as a standing audit step (one page in twenty).

title: Markdown extension: shorthand syntax that auto-links to an anchored target
description:
Writing a long document with a reference inventory means hand-writing the same
`[_Politics_](http://classics.mit.edu/Aristotle/politics.html)` link at every
mention. Want a shorthand that resolves to a declared target instead.

## Shape

Some special syntax at the call site, e.g. `{{politics}}` or `[[politics]]`, that
resolves to a target declared once — either an anchor elsewhere in the same
document, or a URL declared in a frontmatter/definition block. Exact syntax is
open; it must not collide with `[label](href)`, `[^footnote]`, or the existing
`{#id}` anchor marker.

## Prerequisite: `{#id}` anchors on list items

`split-trailing-anchor` (md.scm:267) already parses a trailing `{#id}` marker, but
it is only wired into headings (md.scm:89) and paragraphs (md.scm:288). List items
do not support it.

This matters because reference inventories are lists. In
`templates/bible/theology/monarchy/outline/index.md` the Part IX inventory is an
ordered list of ~150 works, and the only linkable targets are the seven `###`
subsection headings. Body citations therefore link to a whole subsection instead of
to the entry for the work being cited. Per-item anchors are what makes the
shorthand actually precise.

## Also worth deciding

Whether the shorthand's link text comes from the target (so the label is written
once) or is supplied at the call site, e.g. `[[politics|_Politics_ III.12]]`.
Citations frequently need a locator that the target does not carry.

## Motivation

The monarchy outline currently has ~86 hand-written citation links in its body.
Every one of them was applied mechanically and every one has to be maintained by
hand when a URL changes.

## Related

Follows the same "make prose into links without markdown syntax" goal as the
confession auto-linking bead, but it is generic rather than domain-specific.
notes: Implemented as CommonMark reference links rather than a bespoke [[key]] syntax: [label][key], [label][] and shortcut [label], with [key]: url "title" definitions. Standard markdown already solves 'declare a destination once, cite it many times', so no new syntax was invented and other tooling understands the result. An unresolved key keeps its literal text, which is what leaves the outline's [CLAIM]/[EV]/[GAP] markers untouched. Prerequisite shipped too: {#id} anchors now work on list items (split-trailing-anchor was already there, only wired to headings and paragraphs), so a reference definition can point at a single inventory entry.

title: Support footnotes in the markdown renderer
description:
The markdown renderer has no footnote support, so both halves of the syntax render
as literal text.

## Current behavior

`templates/bible/theology/monarchy/draft/index.md` uses seven footnotes. Rendering
it emits the raw markers verbatim — `[^1]` through `[^7]` each appear twice in the
output HTML (once at the call site, once in the Notes section) with no links and no
`<a>` tags at all.

## Scope

- Inline reference `[^label]` becomes a superscript link to the definition.
- Definition line `[^label]: text` is collected out of the body flow.
- Definitions render as an ordered list at the end of the document, each with a
  back-link to its call site.
- Definition bodies go through `parse-inline` (they contain emphasis and links —
  see the draft's Notes section).
- Labels are arbitrary strings, not just integers; number the rendered output by
  order of first reference rather than by label.
- Unreferenced definitions and undefined references should degrade to plain text
  rather than erroring.

## Implementation notes

- `parse-inline` (md.scm:143) is where the `[^label]` call site is recognized; it
  must be attempted before `parse-inline-link-at`, since both start with `[`.
- Collection is a document-level concern, so the definition pass belongs in
  `parse-markdown` / `md->html` rather than inline parsing.
- Generated ids must not collide with `text->id` heading anchors; prefix them
  (`fn-1`, `fnref-1`).
- Add a fixture pair under `scripts/lib/sxml/test/md/` and regenerate with
  `make test/regenerate`.

title: Support tables in the markdown renderer
description:
`parse-markdown` (`scripts/lib/md.scm:293`) handles headings, ordered/unordered
lists, fenced code, blockquotes and paragraphs. There is no table support, so
GitHub-flavored pipe tables render as literal text with visible `|` characters.

## Scope

Parse GFM pipe tables into `(table (thead ...) (tbody ...))` SXML:

```
| Author | Work | Date |
| ------ | ---- | ---- |
| Aristotle | _Politics_ | c. 350 BCE |
```

- Header row, delimiter row, body rows.
- Honor the delimiter row's alignment colons (`:--`, `:-:`, `--:`) as `style="text-align:..."`
  or an alignment class.
- Cell contents go through `parse-inline`, so emphasis and links work inside cells.
- Ragged rows: pad or truncate to the header's column count rather than erroring.

## Notes

- `markdownlint` config already sets MD013 `line_length: 120`; wide tables will
  trip it, so check whether MD013's `tables: false` option should be set in
  `.markdownlint.yaml`.
- The theme stylesheet (`/shared/styles/openword-theme.css`) has no table styling
  yet — needs at least borders and cell padding, and horizontal scroll on narrow
  viewports.
- Add a fixture pair under `scripts/lib/sxml/test/md/` and regenerate with
  `make test/regenerate`.

## Motivation

The monarchy research references are CSVs served as raw asset downloads
(`assets/bible/theology/monarchy/research/references/*.csv`). With table support
they could render as readable on-page tables instead.

title: Auto-link confession notations the way scripture references are linked
description:
`scripts/lib/md.scm` already turns bare scripture references in prose into links:
`linkify-scripture` (md.scm:533-577) walks the parsed SXML, matches book names via
`match-book-at`, and emits anchors against `%scripture-base-url` using
`chapter-anchor` / `verse-anchor`. Pages opt out with `scripture-links: false` in
frontmatter.

Do the same for confessional citations, so writing `1689 ch. 23` or `WCF 22.3` in
prose produces a link with no markdown syntax.

## Forms to recognize

- Second London Baptist Confession: `1689 ch. 23`, `LBCF 23`, `LBCF 23.4`, `2LBCF 24.1`
- Westminster Confession: `WCF 22`, `WCF 23.3`, `Westminster Confession ch. 22`
- Catechisms: Baptist Catechism (1695) and Heidelberg by question number (`HC Q.101`)

Chapter-only and chapter.paragraph should both work, matching how the scripture
linker handles chapter vs. verse.

## Prerequisite

There is nothing in the repo to link *to* — the reference CSVs under
`assets/bible/theology/monarchy/research/references/` contain no confessional
documents. This needs a decision first:

1. Host the confession texts as site content (mirrors the Bible versions approach,
   gives stable in-site anchors, most work), or
2. Link out to canonical public texts (fast, but no anchors per paragraph).

Option 1 is what makes the scripture linker work well and is probably the right
target.

## Reuse notes

`linkify-scripture-node` deliberately skips URLs, existing links, code spans, raw
passthrough, and headings (md.scm:558-573) — a confession linker must respect the
same exclusions, so factor that traversal rather than duplicating it.

## Motivation

`templates/bible/theology/monarchy/outline/index.md` cites the 1689 and Westminster
about 25 times in prose. Those are currently hand-linked to a section anchor, which
is a workaround, not a destination.
notes: Links out to baptistconfession.org, which hosts one paragraph per page. NOTE: the wcf1646 prefix in the original request 404s; the live path is /wcf/{ch}.{par}. Confirmed by chapter count -- /33.1 is 404 (1689 has 32 chapters) while /wcf/33.1 is 200 (WCF has 33). A chapter-only citation links to that chapter's first paragraph, since the site publishes no chapter-level page (/23 is 404). All 5 URLs the site now emits were checked live and return 200. The IX.2 research gap is still open: this links out, it does not add confessional sources to the repo.

title: GSB data: word and post columns of NT gsb/greek tables are not NFC
description: After ursinia-vff.9 the lemma column is NFC, but Nestle-derived word text still has oxia (41660 NT word cells) and 3341 post cells are not NFC (likely ano teleia U+0387 / Greek question mark U+037E, which NFC maps to U+00B7 / ';'). gsb/README.md says tables are NFC. Fix would be string-normalize-nfc on the split-punct parts in read-nestle (scripts/gsb-build.scm) then make gsb; check that the LXX spelling/form tables (spelling-key, fold-key) and TR accent repair still give the same results, and decide whether changing visible punctuation code points is wanted.

title: GSB: owner ruling on readable-layer words a modern reader may not understand (Gen 1-3, John 1)
description: Candidate list from the readable-avoid work (2026-11-26): behold, abyss, luminaries/illumination, firmament (owner considered a replacement, kept for now), unfurnished, invisible, sowable/sowing seed, vegetation of grass, according to kind/similarity, four-footed things, collections of the waters, gathering, carbuncle, leek-green stone, trance, prudent, enmity, watch (3:15), turning (3:16), be lord over, sorrows, tunics, sanctified, genesis, paradise of delight, soul (animals), seed, sides, creeping things. Each rejected word goes in gsb/lexicon/readable-avoid.scm with its replacement; make gsb/lint enforces it.

title: GSB: translation format cannot express discontinuous segments or partly-supplied segments
description: From the Genesis 1-3 pilot (ursinia-vff.4): (1) one Greek word rendered by discontinuous English ('Let [a] firmament come to be', 'sent him out'); (2) genitive 'of' + supplied article ('of [the] field'), since a segment cannot be partly bracketed; (3) punctuation after a supplied word ('[land];'). Workarounds used are listed in gsb/translation/01-gen/book.scm. Owner to decide whether to extend the format (e.g. allow a bracketed article inside a segment, or a segment continuation marker).
notes: Done (agent, 2026-11-26). Format: (cont N) continues word N's English in a later segment; [supplied] words allowed inside a segment with Greek (exempt from gloss/article checks); a wholly supplied segment may carry punctuation outside the brackets ('[one].'); a bare word number now means the lemma's first (default) sense; make gsb/uses LEMMA=... lists uses. Site: translation-json takes senses from verse-uses (honors lemma overrides, cont refs), adds a 5th [cont n...] element; chapters-of groups by chapter in first-appearance order. Applied in Gen 1:3,6,9,11,14,20,22,24; 2:5,23; 3:7,23 (notes updated). No concordance reorder needed: every multi-sense lemma already lists its established sense first. Owner to look at: 3:23 literal now reads 'sent him out out of the paradise' (ἐξ- of the compound plus ἐκ); 1:9 also moved to subject-first ('Let the water ... be gathered', 'let the dry [land] appear;') for consistency with 1:3.

title: GSB: checker rule for keep-the-ambiguity (names/pronouns not in the Greek)
description: Flag a literal segment aligned to οὗτος/ἐκεῖνος whose text has a personal pronoun or name and no 'this/that/these/those'; flag a proper name (gloss of a sense named 'name', or God/Lord) in a literal or aligned-readable segment whose refs lack that lemma; for plain-string readable, flag when a name occurs more often than in the literal layer. Found feasible during the Genesis 1-3 pilot (ursinia-vff.4).
notes: Done (agent, 2026-11-26). Rules in check-chapter (scripts/lib/gsb-translation.scm), tested: (1) demonstrative (οὗτος/ἐκεῖνος/ὅδε) aligned to English with a personal pronoun or name and no this/that/these/those -> error (literal and aligned readable; literal counts the word's (cont N) parts); (2) a name (capitalized gloss of a sense named name, or God/Lord) in a segment whose Greek lacks that lemma -> error, supplied segments included; (3) plain readable: a name more often than in the literal -> error; literal demonstrative rendered this/that/these/those but readable has none of those words -> warning only. Drafts: 0 errors; 1 warning, Gen 3:17 (readable drops 'of this' τούτου: 'from which alone'). Known blind spot: the warning is fooled by an unrelated 'that' (Gen 3:11 readable also drops τούτου μόνου but says 'that you are naked'). Genesis readables are plain strings, so rules 1-2 on the readable layer only bite in John 1.

title: GSB data: lemma column in gsb/greek/*.tsv is not NFC (oxia, e.g. ἀρχή as U+1F75)
description: gsb/README.md says tables are NFC, but Nestle-derived lemmas keep Greek-extended oxia (john.1.1#2 lemma ends in U+1F75; NFC is U+03AE). gsb-check, gsb-site and gsb.js normalize on lookup as a workaround. Fix in gsb-build (string-normalize-nfc the lemma), then make gsb.
close_reason: read-nestle in scripts/gsb-build.scm NFC-normalizes the Nestle lemma; rebuilt gsb/greek and gsb/lexicon/strongs.tsv (lemma columns now NFC); test added. Side effect: two LXX verb/noun ties (-σει) now break the other way by code point order: gen.3.15#26 τηρήσει became τήρησις (pinned back to τηρέω in the translation) and gen.16.11#25 ταπεινώσει became ταπείνωσις (correct there). lxx-coverage.tsv unchanged.
